source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.5.3 Task Scheduling using a Queue (PDF 104, printed 101). Short question 6 is answered.

blocks.text: Task scheduling is like a doctor's clinic. Tasks are like patients waiting their turn; the queue is the waiting list that keeps them in order of arrival. When a new task arrives, for example when you press Print, it is enqueued at the back; when the computer is ready it dequeues the task at the front, like the doctor calling the next patient. The queue makes sure tasks are processed in order, none is skipped, and work is handled efficiently and fairly.
